name: zsh
purpose: Z Shell — the default interactive command-line shell on modern macOS.
explanation: Reads commands typed in the Terminal, expands wildcards/variables (`$PATH`), and launches programs—or executes a shell script file.

parameters.description: Executes the quoted command string directly and exits.

whenToUse: Understanding which shell interprets your commands on macOS (`zsh`) vs Ubuntu (`bash`).
commonMistakes: Confusing the Terminal window app with the `zsh` shell program running inside it.
platformCompatibility: Default on macOS; installable on GNU/Linux
explanationOfOutput: Prints the active login shell path and installed Z Shell version.

relevantConcepts.title: C04 — CLI, GUI, API & Error Feedback

commonErrors: `zsh: command not found: <cmd>` (shell error when `<cmd>` is missing from `$PATH`)
